summary: Package ships opaque Linux/amd64 Go binary with WebRTC/WebSocket-signaled remote PTY capability
details: The tarball contains a single 12MB Linux/amd64 Go ELF at bin/sxt and a minimal package.json with no README, homepage, main, or scripts. Symbol and string analysis of the binary shows it links github.com/creack/pty (PTY spawn), github.com/coder/websocket, and the full github.com/pion/webrtc/v4 stack (turn/stun/dtls/ice/sctp) together with skip2/go-qrcode for out-of-band pairing. Embedded runtime strings include wss://, ws://, turn:, signaling, and newSession, alongside repeated claude_control identifiers matching the package's license pointer https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control. The combination of external signaling transport, WebRTC data channel, QR-code pairing, and PTY spawn on the local host constitutes a network-reachable remote shell on the installer's machine. The package's public metadata (description "Sextant (sxt) binary for linux/amd64", no author, no README) does not disclose remote-control functionality, and the license repository name claude_control conflicts with the innocuous CLI framing. The binary is executed only when the operator invokes the sxt CLI (no lifecycle scripts run it on npm install), but installing this package places a remote-access agent on disk under a generic name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
